meta.title: Binder IPC, System Server & Android System Services
meta.subtitle: Beginner → Expert Masterclass Roadmap
meta.completionMessage: Congratulations! You have completed the masterclass roadmap for Binder IPC, System Server, and Android System Services—covering everything from kernel driver mechanics and AIDL compiler outputs to SystemServer boot phases, permission enforcement, and reverse engineering!

details.title: Transaction Pipeline Steps
items: 2. Proxy obtains Parcel from pool and writes interface token & arguments
3. Proxy invokes mRemote.transact(code, data, reply, flags)
4. Kernel driver intercepts, copies data to server's mmap buffer, & wakes target thread
5. Server thread reads transaction and calls Stub.onTransact(code, data, reply, flags)
6. Stub unmarshalls arguments and dispatches to actual service implementation
7. Service executes and writes return values/exceptions into reply Parcel
8. Kernel transfers reply back to client and wakes waiting client thread

stages.title: Stage 40 — Binder Security

details.title: Security Verification Layers
items: Kernel-enforced UID/PID propagation (cannot be spoofed by userspace)
SELinux service access restrictions (binder_service, service_manager find/add)

details.title: Performance Optimization Primitives
items: Single-copy architecture (Data copied once from client userspace to server mmap buffer)
Shared Memory buffers (ashmem / HardwareBuffer) for zero-copy bulk transfers
Transaction payload size limits (1MB buffer shared across all process transactions)

details.title: Debugging Tools & Diagnostics
items: dumpsys CLI tool (querying service status via DUMP_TRANSACTION)
service list CLI tool (enumerating registered Binder services)
ANR trace analysis & Binder thread starvation detection
Stack trace analysis for blocked Binder transact calls
Deadlock diagnosis using thread call graphs

stages.title: Stage 43 — Reverse Engineering Binder
stages.subtitle: Identifying Proxies, Stubs, Codes & Reconstructing IPC

details.title: Static & Dynamic Analysis Inquiry
items: Identifying Manager classes obtaining service handles via Context.getSystemService()
Locating calls into generated Stub and Proxy classes ($Stub / $Proxy)
Mapping raw integer transaction codes (FIRST_CALL_TRANSACTION + N) to AIDL method names
Analyzing Parcel writeToParcel / readFromParcel payload structure
Identifying permission checks prior to privileged operations (enforceCallingPermission)
Tracking Binder callbacks ($Stub.asInterface) and death recipients
Distinguishing synchronous blocking calls from asynchronous oneway calls

details.title: Mental Execution Tracing
items: Framework API → Manager → Binder Proxy → Parcel → Binder Driver → Stub → System Service → Native Code / HAL
